title: The tortoise who talked too much.
lines: This is a story from India, from the old book of animal stories.
By a beautiful lake, with lotus flowers and tall reeds, lived a tortoise.
Their names were Hamsa and Hamsi.
Every day the geese came to the lake.
Then the three of them sat in the sun and talked.
He talked about the weather, about the fish, about the clouds.
He talked in the morning and in the evening.
He even talked while he was eating.
The geese thought he was very sweet.
But sometimes they said: Kambu, you should listen sometimes too.
One summer it didn't rain at all.
Day after day the sun shone.
And the lake got smaller and smaller.
And then there was only mud.
We have to leave, they said.
Behind the mountains there is a big lake.
I'll stay here, in the dry mud.
They didn't want to leave their friend behind.
We'll take a strong stick, she said.
I'll hold one end in my beak.
Hamsi will hold the other end.
And you, Kambu, bite the middle of the stick.
Then we'll fly you with us!
There's just one thing, she said.
You must keep your mouth shut.
Because if you open your mouth, you'll let go of the stick.
I won't say anything, he promised.
They looked for a strong stick.
The geese each took an end in their beaks.
They flew up into the sky, with Kambu hanging from the stick.
The houses looked like little blocks.
He wanted so badly to say something.
But he kept his mouth shut.
Children were playing in the street.
Two geese are carrying a tortoise!
He didn't like them laughing at all.
He wanted to shout something back.
He wanted to say: I'm not a strange bird!
I'm a tortoise, and these are my friends!
He couldn't hold it in any longer.
And he let go of the stick.
Luckily they were flying very low, over a big haystack.
Kambu fell right into the soft hay.
He wasn't hurt, just a bit startled.
His shell was full of bits of straw.
I should have kept my mouth shut.
But this time don't listen to the children, okay?
And this time he didn't say a thing.
Not even when the cows mooed at him.
At last they landed at the big lake.
The water was blue and cool.
And then he was allowed to talk again.
He talked about the journey all afternoon.
Sometimes it's clever to be quiet for a while.
